newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourses up,Ldn climbs on oil sector gain.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourses up,Ldn climbs on oil sector gain.

text.p: European stocks held their gains on Tuesday despite an unsteady start on Wall Street, with London climbing nearly one percent on the back of a strong showing by oil companies.

In currency markets, the dollar jumped a pfennig after the Bundesbank on Tuesday kept its key repo rate steady at 3.00 percent although many traders took the view that the threat of rising German rates remained in the market.

The stronger showing on European bourses followed Monday's lacklustre start to the week when investors were shaken by a sharp Wall Street fall on Friday, leading to fears that the recent bull run was petering out.

London led the way on Tuesday, climbing 45.2 points to 5077.2 on the FTSE 100 index in the afternoon, shrugging off a negative start on Wall Street, with gains in British Petroleum and Shell outpacing a sell-off in pharmaceutical stocks.

Investors ignored a stronger-than -forecast British inflation figure for July, and bought shares in retail stocks like Dixons amid evidence that windfall flotation payments were still boosting sales of big-ticket items.
"The drugs have underperformed but I think that is a little overdone...and the market looks pretty firm," one trader said. "
The FTSE 100 index, which closed only just in the plus column on Monday, was at one stage trading only a few below its all-time peak of 5,086.8 set last Thursday

Paris, which ended down on Monday, had a volatile morning. Stocks climbed 0.89 percent at the opening on bullish sentiment after the Bundesbank move but lost most of the gains. A modest pick-up on Wall Street by mid-afternoon failed to help.
In Frankfurt, floor trade stocks closed up 0.7 percent, encouraged by the dollar's recent strength, which boosts prospects for exporters. After-hours deals on the computerised IBIS inxex were up 0.8.
The currency markets were firmly focused on the Bundesbank with traders digesting the effect of the "no-change" rate move.
The dollar staged a minor rally after on the Bundesbank's announcement but it failed to build up monetum during the session and paused at 1.8650 marks, up about a pfennig on Monday's close.
"Initially the dollar benefited when the Bundesbank left the repo rate at three percent, but it didn't go too far," said Lisa Finstrom, senior currency analyst at Smith Barney in New York.
Few market players expected to see either an outright hike in the German repo rate or a switch to variable-rate tenders, but the markets were kept guessing over the Bundesbank's next move.
"It means we'll have to do this Bundesbank watch again next week," said Marc Chandler, senior currency analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

The British pound, which moved in sympathy with the dollar, dipped against the U.S. currency and the mark in mid-afternoon after remarks by a government official that British inflation would drop soon, discouraging talk of higher interest rates.

Sterling fell by 1.5 cents to $1.5760 and by a pfennig to 2.9370 as Junior Treasury minister Geoffrey Robinson said underlying inflation would drop back to the government's 2.5 percent target in the next couple of months.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.8650 marks and 116.07 yen, compared with 1.8543 and 115.78 in late trading on Monday
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 45.2 points at 5,077.2.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index closed up 29.96 points at 4,363.09 in bourse floor trade.
PARIS - The CAC-40 index was up 9.63 points at 2,992.42
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $326.15 an ounce, down on Monday's London close of $327.25. Silver was down a cent at $4.42.
